page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.xlarge is an Arm-based general-purpose virtual machine provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.8 GHz Ampere Altra processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, offering a 1:4 allocation ratio paired with 16.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per core). The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage solutions, and features a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reflects mid-tier performance across raw compute and memory throughput metrics. In synthetic stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves average results for both single-core (1789.99) and multi-core (7136.84) execution. Uncached memory read (50.64 GB/sec) and write (29.82 GB/sec) bandwidth metrics on 256 MB blocks also place within the average tier. PassMark database operations hold a middle-tier score of 2947.42, and small-model LLM text generation reaches an average rate of 104.82 tokens/sec.

Performance constraints appear primarily in specialized workloads. The absence of x86 vector extensions and specialized matrix instructions results in weaker scores on the PassMark CPU suite (overall score of 3200.71, with encryption placing in the bottom 10% at 649.99). Additionally, caching, compression benchmarks (23.76 GB/sec for gzip), and Redis SET throughput (5.78 million ops/sec) rank in the lower quartile. The 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth limits high-throughput data transfer requirements.

This hardware balance renders ecs.g6r.xlarge suitable for standard general-purpose computing tasks that require dedicated Arm resources without extreme compute or high-speed local IO requirements. It is best applied to standard web serving, mid-range relational or operational databases, background queue workers, and lightweight containerized microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by a 2.8 GHz Ampere Altra Arm processor. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs, 16.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU), and a 1 Gbps baseline network connection, configured without local storage or GPUs. Benchmark evaluation reveals mid-range results in stress-ng compute tests and uncached memory bandwidth, alongside average performance in database operations and lightweight LLM text generation. However, it displays lower relative performance in hardware-accelerated encryption, single-threaded compression, and in-memory key-value processing. The instance delivers a balanced resource profile suitable for operational databases, microservices, containerized workloads, and general cloud infrastructure services that do not require high network throughput or local NVMe storage.
